name: Diffuse Lighting Models
text:
# Diffuse Lighting Models


## Overview
Diffuse Lighting Models compute surface illumination for ray-marched geometry and [Signed Distance Fields](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md) (SDFs) by evaluating the geometric relationship between surface normals and light directions [S2, S3, S10, unofficial]. The family encompasses pure diffuse models, Phong and Blinn-Phong variants that incorporate specular highlights, and [Gouraud shading](#4645-gouraud-shading.md) which interpolates vertex colors [S1, S2, S3, S10, unofficial].

## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### [Phong Shading with SDF Normals](1977-phong-shading-with-sdf-normals.md)
Applies the Phong reflection model to SDF surfaces. Computes normals via the SDF gradient and accumulates diffuse and specular contributions per fragment. Differs from [Lambertian Lighting in SDF](2023-lambertian-lighting-in-sdf.md) by including specular highlights, and from [Blinn-Phong Shading in Volume Rendering](2809-blinn-phong-shading-in-volume-rendering.md) by using the exact reflected light vector rather than the half-vector approximation. Choose when specular highlights are required alongside diffuse shading.

### [Lambertian Lighting in SDF](2023-lambertian-lighting-in-sdf.md)
Computes diffuse illumination for SDF surfaces by evaluating the dot product between the surface normal and the light direction. Solves shading without explicit mesh topology by deriving normals via finite differences. Unlike [Sphere Tracing Basics](52-sphere-tracing-basics.md), which returns a flat base color, this method integrates a light direction and color.

### [Blinn-Phong Shading in Volume Rendering](2809-blinn-phong-shading-in-volume-rendering.md)
Applies Blinn-Phong lighting during ray-marching to compute surface normals and lighting contributions for volumetric data. Distinguishes itself from simple [alpha-blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md) by incorporating specular highlights and diffuse shading based on estimated surface normals, providing greater depth cues. Choose for volumetric data where normals are approximated via central differences of intensity gradients.

### [Gouraud Shading](4645-gouraud-shading.md)
Computes colors for each vertex based on a lighting model and vertex normals, then linearly interpolates colors across the facet. Choose for performance-critical applications where per-fragment [normal calculation](#857-finite-difference-gradient-estimation.md) is too expensive, though it may exhibit shading artifacts on large polygons.

### Flat Shading
#### definition
A shading model assuming uniform lighting where light surrounds an object equally in all directions [S1, unofficial].
#### code
`glShadeModel(GL_FLAT)` [S1, unofficial]
#### pitfall
Flat shading diminishes the three dimensionality of the scene [S1, unofficial].

## Background
Diffuse lighting models originate from early computer graphics shading techniques, specifically within the OpenGL specification which defined flat and Gouraud (smooth) [shading models](#837-shading-models.md) [S1, unofficial]. The specification notes that flat shading assumes uniform lighting, while smooth shading assumes directional light, requiring normal vectors to estimate reflected light fractions [S1, unofficial].
